title: Master Documentation and Manuscript Update
note: browser frontend is spec-level, backend API tested; this is the master documentation / manuscript phase
negative_results: No cwatlas code, tests, schemas, __init__, claims, pyproject, or build_meta were modified; documentation only.
No source vector has earned the CALIBRATED_MAPPING class; it is evidence-gated and unreachable without a prospective known-destination challenge that has not been passed.
The manuscript records what round-trips exactly (CW-GEO-1, CW-HCM-ICO in System 1) and what stays alias-only or refuses (the legacy codecs in System 2); it claims nothing physical.

claims.statement: The CW Atlas is a bidirectional geocoder whose two systems are firewalled: a canonical reversible geocoder (CANONICAL_ROUND_TRIP) and a source-vector hypothesis decoder (at most MATHEMATICAL_TRANSLATION), with no promotion between them.
A source vector does not identify a real location (claims.refuse_source_as_geographic).
Stonehenge or any other named site has not been decoded from the vector family (claims.refuse_site_decoded).
The coordinate system does not control gravity, portals, craft, or consciousness (claims.refuse_control_claim).
A close arithmetic match does not establish intended encoding (claims.refuse_close_match_as_intent).
A public patent does not validate a secret craft programme (claims.refuse_patent_as_craft_validation).
A legacy alias set is not forced to one pin (claims.refuse_alias_as_unique).
A reversible canonical round-trip does not prove a source vector's meaning (claims.refuse_synthetic_codec_as_source_meaning).
A map pin is not produced without a declared CRS and epoch (claims.refuse_pin_without_crs_epoch).

privacy_check: CLEAN - synthetic fixtures only, no private inputs
